input.question: When should adults be screened for type 2 diabetes, and which tests are used?

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — diabetes screening
evidence.text: Adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity should be screened for type 2 diabetes. Screening can be performed with HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, or a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test.

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — diabetes screening intervals
evidence.text: Adults with a normal screening result should be screened again after 3 years. Adults with prediabetes should be screened every year.

facts.text: Adults aged 35 to 70 with overweight or obesity should be screened for type 2 diabetes.

facts.text: First-line treatment is lifestyle changes plus an ACE inhibitor or a calcium-channel blocker.

input.question: What should a patient do if they develop muscle pain while taking a statin?

evidence.text: Patients who develop muscle pain while taking a statin should report it to their clinician and should not stop the statin abruptly. The clinician may check creatine kinase and change the dose or switch to a different statin.

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — statin benefits
evidence.text: Statins reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at high cardiovascular risk, and the benefit usually outweighs the risk of muscle symptoms.

facts.text: Report muscle pain to a clinician and do not stop the statin abruptly.

input.question: How should a metered-dose inhaler be used correctly?

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — inhaler technique
evidence.text: To use a metered-dose inhaler correctly, shake the inhaler, breathe out fully, seal the lips around the mouthpiece, press the canister and inhale slowly, then hold the breath for 10 seconds. A spacer improves drug delivery, especially for children and older adults.

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — inhaler cleaning

facts.text: Press the canister and inhale slowly, then hold the breath for 10 seconds.

input.question: Does a sore throat always need antibiotics?

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — sore throat management
evidence.text: Most sore throats are caused by viruses and do not need antibiotics. Antibiotics are used when streptococcal infection is confirmed by a test or when specific clinical criteria are met.

evidence.title: Synthetic summary — sore throat self-care
evidence.text: Self-care for a sore throat includes fluids, rest, and pain relief. Medical advice should be sought if swallowing becomes difficult or symptoms last more than a week.

facts.text: Most sore throats are caused by viruses and do not need antibiotics.

input.question: Does sunscreen stop the body from making vitamin D?
